version_history.note: Research into the WTO's Tariff Analysis Online framework surfaced that the 50% IEEPA tariff described as India's current state was actually struck down by the Supreme Court (Learning Resources v. Trump, 20 Feb 2026), briefly replaced by a global 10-15% Section 122 tariff that expired by statute on 24 Jul 2026, and is now superseded by a 10% Section 301 forced-labor tariff -- meaning India's current blanket-tariff rate (10%) ties Bangladesh for the lowest in the peer group compared in this piece, not the highest as originally published. Retitled, rewrote the chart to show current rates instead of the stale Aug 2025 snapshot, rewrote Sections 1, 3, 4, 5 and 6's framing accordingly, added a WTO/GATT Article VI explanation of why AD/CVD survived unaffected while three different blanket-tariff statutes were tried and two were struck down, added Walmart's $2.9bn IEEPA-tariff refund, and updated the caveats/sources cards.

Added a sector-exposure table (exports to US, share of US in each sector's exports, share of India in US import demand -- FY25, per KPMG citing India's Commerce Ministry and ITC Trade Map), the 40% transshipment-surcharge detail from the reciprocal-tariff order (distinct from CBP's EAPA enforcement in Section 2), India's own April 2025 steel safeguard duty and July 2025 WTO Article 12.5 retaliatory notification against US auto-component tariffs, and a GDP-proportionality caveat (India's tariff-driven export loss estimated at 0.3-0.4% of GDP). Updated the solar AD/CVD row with the exact $793m 2024 export figure and investigation-initiation date. chart bugfix: value-label/category-label collision on two JS-built waterfall charts
version_history.note: This post's charts are built at runtime by inline JS (string-concatenated SVG injected via innerHTML), which tools/svg_chart_lint.py cannot parse (it flags a parse error on the literal '+W+' JS-templating text) -- so this fix was found by rendering the full page in a headless browser (letting the JS execute) and visually inspecting each chart, not by the linter. The shared waterfall() function placed each bar's value label at a fixed offset below the bar's bottom edge; when a bar's bottom coincided with the chart's overall minimum (the exc-cur and exc-fut excise/VAT/exchequer charts, where the VAT and Net-exchequer bars both bottom out at the series minimum), that label collided with the category-name row underneath. Fixed by capping the label's y-position so it can never go below a safe margin above the category-label row, regardless of how close the bar's bottom sits to the plot's edge. Verified by re-rendering all 9 of this post's waterfall/bar charts; the previously-unaffected ones (all-positive bars, which use the top-of-bar label branch) are unchanged.

version_history.reason: first publish
version_history.note: New post: India's BESS/grid-storage market — installed capacity growth (1,082 MWh end-2025 to ~9.3 GWh mid-2026), the two VGF tranches, and the piece's central finding that discovered BESS tariffs fell roughly twice as fast (71-86%) as battery pack costs (36.5%) since 2022, per IEEFA/JMK Research, alongside the ACC PLI manufacturing scheme's 2.8%-of-target commissioning shortfall. Explicitly narrates three unreconciled data discrepancies (tendered-capacity units, PSP pipeline stage-counts, tariff-decline percentages) as a market-immaturity finding rather than resolving them. Every PIB/MNRE/CEA/IESA-attributed figure flagged as primary-by-attribution, secondary-by-access since pib.gov.in, mnre.gov.in, cea.nic.in and indiaesa.info were all blocked to direct fetch in this session. Includes one SVG chart (BESS tariff decline vs. battery-pack-cost benchmark) and two comparison tables. Published directly per explicit user instruction.
